fact: ActuNiger says the AES passport launch came a few months after the launch of the biometric national identity card (CNIB).

Niger opened enrolment for the biometric national identity card CNIB AES in Agadez, collecting fingerprints and biometrics locally and sending files to Niamey for printing, with a five-year validity, per the Journal du Niger.
Niger launched a new-generation national identity card for which President Tiani enrolled first, shortly before the passport launch reported 11 September 2026.
Niger approved two draft decrees in December introducing electronic AES passports and AES biometric national identity cards to replace the ECOWAS ENBIC card.

Niger is modernising its national identification system under WURI-Niger with World Bank support, with a first registration phase to start soon in Niamey and extend to the regions, says the director general of territorial administration.

The government is putting a new biometric national identity card into circulation and moving to biometric enrolment of the population and constitution of the National Population Register, said the Agadez governor.
Niger created ANEI by decree n°2026-242 and announced a forthcoming National Population Register, a central secured database to give each citizen a unique identifier.

The Interior Ministry said on 12 August 2026 that the Registre National de la Population will become the single base to identify and authenticate each citizen by a personal identifier, with deployment starting in Niamey in the coming weeks and national extension from 2027 under the future ANEI.

Le Sahel reports the restructured WURI project is building a National Population Register (RNP) to identify and authenticate individuals, with enrolment to start in Niamey's five arrondissements, and the ANEI agency created by decree of 22 April 2026.
The WURI-Niger project says its MOSIP-based identification pilot in Tanout commune, Zinder region, enrolled 500 people ahead of national implementation, financed by the World Bank.

The WURI-Niger coordinator says the World Bank-financed project, under the Interior ministry, is setting up a system giving each person a unique identifier number (NIU), and procurement of the national biometric identification information system is being prepared.
Niger's Interior Minister signed an MoU on 27 June 2025 under a public-private partnership to launch a new electronic national ID card meeting international security standards.
